one_line: Dalavoy and chief minister of the Madurai Nayakas, architect of the palayam system and patron of the Thousand-Pillared Hall.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, medium height, sturdy build with a disciplined, administrative bearing.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium brown South Indian complexion, high cheekbones, neatly trimmed moustache, faint lines at the eyes from concentration, default expression calm and authoritative with a measured, thoughtful gaze.
appearance.hair: Straight black hair pulled back into a tight low knot at the nape of the neck, front hair combed back from the forehead, no shaved portions; simple white cotton headcloth folded as a narrow band and tied around the head like a turban-ring, leaving the top mostly flat.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate 16th-century South Indian elite attire: a finely woven off-white cotton veshti (dhoti) wrapped to ankle length with a neat pleated fan in front and a pale gold border; upper body covered by a close-fitting, elbow-length white cotton angarkha-style tunic with a slight overlap at the chest; over this a rich deep-maroon silk angavastram draped over the left shoulder and across the torso, its border in muted gold with small repeating floral motifs; simple leather sandals on the feet; jewellery limited to a thin gold chain around the neck, a small cylindrical talisman pendant, and modest gold studs in the ears, emphasizing sobriety rather than ostentation.
appearance.signature: A long palm-leaf manuscript roll bound with a dark red cloth and a slender wooden writing stylus tucked alongside, held in his left hand as the symbol of his administrative and fiscal innovations.

ref_desc: Ariyanatha Mudaliar appears as a sturdy, medium-brown man with an oval face, black hair in a low knot with a simple white headband, wearing an off-white dhoti, white tunic and deep-maroon angavastram with pale gold borders, modest gold jewellery, and carrying a bound palm-leaf manuscript with stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Ariyanatha Mudaliar: a late-middle-aged, medium-height, sturdy South Indian man with an oval face, medium brown complexion, high cheekbones and a neat moustache, expression calm and authoritative. His straight black hair is combed back and tied in a tight low knot at the nape, with a simple white cotton headcloth folded into a narrow band encircling his head. He wears an era-accurate off-white cotton dhoti (veshti) to the ankles with a precise front pleat and a pale gold border, a close-fitting elbow-length white cotton tunic covering his torso, and a deep-maroon silk angavastram draped from the left shoulder across his chest, edged in muted gold with subtle repeating floral motifs. His feet have plain leather sandals, and his jewellery is restrained: a thin gold chain with a small talisman pendant at his neck and modest gold ear studs. In his left hand he holds a bound palm-leaf manuscript roll wrapped with dark red cloth, with a slender wooden writing stylus tucked along it as his signature administrative prop. Show him from multiple angles in consistent anime style, emphasizing the fixed face, hair knot and headband, the maroon-and-gold drape over white garments, and the manuscript with stylus, using a palette dominated by deep maroon, off-white, pale gold, dark brown and black.
